title: MEGA.mini: A Universal Generative AI Processor with a New Big/Little Core Architecture for NPU
problem: Generative AI processors must efficiently accelerate both non-diffusion models (VAEs, GANs, transformers) and diffusion models; diffusion models require 25–100x more operations due to iterative inference, creating a computational mismatch for single-architecture designs.
motivation: Generative AI applications (image/text/video creation) are rapidly expanding; efficient processors supporting both NDM and DM workloads enable practical on-device AI assistants.
method: MEGA.mini implements a big/little core architecture where big cores optimize for NDM inference (CNNs, transformers) and little cores handle diffusion model iterative steps; heterogeneous compute fabric scales performance and energy across workload diversity.
key_novelty: Big/little heterogeneous core architecture for NPUs differentiating between computationally-sparse NDMs and iterative-heavy diffusion models.
contributions: Big/little heterogeneous architecture addressing NDM vs. DM computational asymmetry
Unified processor supporting VAEs, GANs, transformers, and diffusion models
Efficient scaling for both high-throughput NDM and iterative DM inference
Universal generative AI processor eliminating separate NDM/DM accelerators
limitations: Specific performance, energy, and area metrics; comparison with state-of-the-art NPUs not provided.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous big/little NPU for unified generative AI (NDM + diffusion) processing
